source.title: Identifying the Training Stop Point with Noisy Labeled Data
source.authors: S. Kamabattula; V. Devarajan; Babak Namazi; Ganesh Sankaranarayanan

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; figures are described but their plotted values are not provided as recoverable numbers.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures clean/noisy label recall and training/test accuracy over training under label noise, a conceptual test of noisy-label learning behavior. It does not reproduce the original random-label experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses the rate of change of training accuracy and reports experiments under symmetric and asymmetric label noise. Its comparisons with prior work and baseline-method results are not rows unless they measure the study's own label-noise behavior.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures clean versus noisy label learning during ordinary training, testing V6, and reports incomplete training fit under partial label corruption, bearing on V4. Its results extend beyond evaluating its stopping algorithm.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose using reductions in training-accuracy changes to locate a stopping region and a heuristic stopping point near maximum test accuracy. They acknowledge that early stopping can exclude harder clean samples learned later.
record.recipe_differences: The study monitors training-accuracy changes and clean/noisy label recall to locate an early stopping point; it does not apply the original random-label memorization intervention.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise type and ratio, dataset, architecture, learning-rate schedule, and AutoTSP thresholds/stop-point choice affect reported outcomes; the authors describe some outcomes as less desirable for harder asymmetric noise and some stop points as earlier than MOTA.

fits_no_version.finding: AutoTSP often selects a stopping point near maximum test accuracy, with performance varying by architecture, noise condition and stopping-rule choices.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-accuracy dynamics can identify useful early stopping points without a clean validation set or known noise ratio.

record.peer_reviewed: 2020 International Conference on Computational Science and Computational Intelligence (CSCI)
record.problems: Results bearing on the trajectories are presented in plots without recoverable numeric values in the supplied text. Experiments use selected noise ratios, not a complete sweep through all corruption levels. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: the relevant clean/noisy recall and accuracy trajectories are figure-only in the supplied text, with no precise values to record. Tables I–III report stopping-method metrics, but do not give training-fit error by noise condition.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error under that labeling, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Time to fit random versus true labels and convergence slowdown as corruption increases.
A corruption sweep extending to completely random labels and steady test-error degradation toward chance across that sweep.
Regularization ablations and generalization after removing regularization.
Learning on a separately fully random-labeled dataset.

missing.what: Final standard-training clean-label recall and label precision in Tables I–III are numerical measurements of ordinary training behavior, not merely stopping-method performance. In particular, Table III reports ResNet32 final clean-label recall of 84.36% on CIFAR-10 and 70.97% on CIFAR-100 with 50% symmetric noise. These establish incomplete training fit. The record's stated omission of figure-only trajectories does not cover these numerical results.
missing.locator: Section V-A, Tables I–III, Standard (LR) and Standard (LP); paragraph introducing ResNet32 results

record.verdict_notes: The absence of recoverable plot coordinates does not prevent qualitative verdicts supported by explicit descriptions of the study's own results. The supporting and limiting V6 trajectories were already declared in rows_left_out, so they are not repeated as missing. No existing rows require correction.

versions.untested_parts: No experiment uses completely random labels or reports whether training error reaches zero or near zero; no test-error-at-chance result is reported.
The study does not compare training time or convergence speed against true-label training, nor report a slowdown factor.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input experiment is reported.

Tests selected synthetic noise ratios and a real-world noisy set, but does not test corruption continuously from none to all or report perfect training fit at each ratio. Relevant plot values are figure-only and not extractable as numbers.
No weight-decay, dropout, or augmentation ablation is reported.

The study compares clean and noisy label recall during training, but does not study completely random labels or establish the claim's broader real-versus-random distinction. Relevant trajectory values are figure-only.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10, 50% symmetric label noise, CNN9 and ResNet110
relationships.reason: Section III and Figure 1 describe clean-label recall increasing faster initially while noisy-label recall remains minimal, followed by increasing noisy-label learning; this verdict uses text because no rows were retained.
relationships.display_finding: Clean-label recall initially increased faster while noisy-label recall remained minimal, followed by increasing learning of noisy labels.
